info.title: com.clodhub/mail
info.description: Transactional email from the shop's server: booking confirmations, gift cards and owner notices. Addresses come from environment variables the settings name, because no setting grammar holds an email address. Every implementation has a simulated mode that keeps messages in an outbox, so the shop and the class checks run without a provider account. Server only.

methods.name: createMail
methods.description: A mail client with the installed settings, or `options.settings` over them: live with the provider, or simulated when `simulate` is true. The addresses are read from the environment when it is created. Returns the client itself, not a promise.

methods.name: Mail.send
methods.description: Sends the message from `from` and resolves to its id. A message outside MailMessage is INVALID_MESSAGE, whatever the configuration, and nothing is sent or kept. A live client without its API key or a from address is NOT_CONFIGURED; the provider refusing the message or not being reached is PROVIDER_ERROR. A simulated client keeps the message in its outbox instead, with or without a from address.

methods.name: Mail.outbox
methods.description: Copies of the last 1,000 messages a simulated client kept, oldest first, each as it was given; always empty for a live client.

methods.name: escapeHtml
methods.description: Text made safe to put in HTML, as element content or a quoted attribute value: & < > " and ' become entities. null and undefined give the empty text; any other value its String form.

methods.name: isEmailAddress
methods.description: Whether the value is an email address as MailMessage takes one.

filename.description: The file name shown to the recipient.

content.description: The file's bytes in base64, padded.

contentType.description: A media type such as image/png.

contentId.description: Makes the attachment an inline image: the HTML shows it with .

oneOf.description: An email address: a local part, @ and a domain with a dot, in ASCII, at most 254 characters, without a name (not Ana <ana@example.com>).

items.description: An email address: a local part, @ and a domain with a dot, in ASCII, at most 254 characters, without a name (not Ana <ana@example.com>).

to.description: One address, or 1 to 50; a provider counts each as one email against its quota.

subject.description: Not only spaces, and no line breaks or other control characters.

html.description: The message as HTML, not only spaces; escape any text it includes with escapeHtml.

text.description: The message as plain text; the provider may derive one from the HTML when it is omitted.

replyTo.description: An email address: a local part, @ and a domain with a dot, in ASCII, at most 254 characters, without a name (not Ana <ana@example.com>).

attachments.description: At most 40,000,000 characters of base64 in all.

env.description: Where the addresses and the API key are read, in the variables the settings name; the server's environment by default.

settings.description: Settings that replace the installed ones, such as fromVariable or senderName.

senderName.description: The name in from, in any characters but control characters, such as the shop's name from its content; it replaces the senderName setting, whose grammar allows only ASCII letters, digits, spaces and hyphens.

fetch.description: The fetch function for provider requests; the global fetch by default. A simulated client never calls it.

simulate.description: Send nothing: every message goes to the client's outbox. For local use and checks.

from.description: The sender as messages carry it: the sender name, then the address the variable fromVariable names in angle brackets (Example Studio <noreply@example.com>). A name with a character other than ASCII letters, digits, spaces and hyphens is in double quotes, with a backslash before each double quote or backslash in it. Empty when the variable holds no email address.

business.description: The shop's own address, from the variable businessVariable names, for the owner's copies and for replies; empty when the variable holds no email address.

InvalidSettings.message: RangeError: a setting outside its grammar, or a senderName option that is empty, over 200 characters or has a control character
